The main takeaway from our work is that

the chloride transporters NKCC1 and KCC2 are expressed in GnRH neurons at all stages of development, but the balance in expression of these transporters changes during development, resulting in depolarizing responses in the embryo and hyperpolarizing responses in adult.

NKCC1 and HCO3 - are the major contributors to depolarization of GnRH neurons by GABAA receptor mediated chloride influx, whereas KCC2 does not contribute to the depolarization in GnRH neurons in any developmental stage.
NKCC1 is expressed in GnRH neurons throughout the life of the animal, and contributes to depolaring GABA responses.
